title: Vow of Teeth
subtitle: An Arranged Marriage Assassin Romantasy
description:
She was paid to kill her husband. He watched her change on their wedding night.

Neela is an odiyan, a guild assassin who becomes a leopard after dark. Sold as a bride to Devan, warden of the hill fort Kettamala, she has forty days before the monsoon seals the Monkey Pass to finish her twelfth contract. Twelve kills buy release: her guild page burned and her birth name returned. She has never known that name.

Devan is quiet, exact and does not lie. He is also the one man alive who saw her turn. In this world, anyone who watches an odiyan change can cage her for life with a single spoken word. He could say it any night. Instead he bars the shutters, kennels the hounds and asks her for nothing. She can't tell whether that is mercy or a hunter's patience.

The guild wants him dead by the new moon, and its enforcer is not a patient man. Someone on the queen's council is selling the passes to raiders. Devan's sister died on his own stairs six years ago. And every night Neela spends beside him puts her cage one careless word closer to his mouth.

Will Neela kill the husband she was sold to, or trust the one man who holds her leash to cut it?

Arranged marriage. Enemies to lovers. Slow burn. Open-door heat and dark edges. Book 1 of The Odiyan Contracts, with a happy-for-now ending and a series question that pulls into book 2.

heat_notes: Open door, moderate: two to three explicit scenes, each changing the bargain between the leads. Consensual, with the heroine setting her own terms.
content_notes: Contract killing and a guild that owns its members; arranged marriage; poisoning and sword violence; animal attacks; the on-page death of a guild-sister and a young guard; caged people whose minds fade; references to a sibling's past murder. No sexual violence on or off the page. The love interest's power over the heroine is treated as harm he names and gives up.
